steps.text: Place ingredients in the pan of the bread machine in the order recommended by the manufacturer. Select dough cycle; press start.

When dough cycle has finished, turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and roll out 3/4 inch thick. Cut out rolls with a 3 to 4 inch diameter biscuit cutter. Place on lightly greased cookie sheets; cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour. Meanwhile, preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bake in preheated oven for 10 to 15 minutes. When rolls are finished baking, brush with melted butter.

raw_recipe.headline: Honey Wheat Sandwich Rolls
raw_recipe.description: The premium taste of these honey wheat rolls may be attributable to the dab of butter within. Let the bread machine do the heavy work before you shape and bake them.

review.reviewBody: I love this recipe. I found the recipe Sunday and have already made 2 batches of rolls and 2 loaves of bread. I don't have a bread machine, so I use my standmixer. I put the dough hook on warm the milk and honey, proof the yeast for 10 min., add the eggs and butter, measure all dry ingredients in a bowl and whisk to make sure distributed, slowly add flour mix in 3 batches.Then I knead with the standmixer 7-10min.To make sure gluten is developed take a golf ball sized piece of dough and stretch in opposite directions using your thumb and forefinger of both hand. If it stretches thin enough to see light through without it tearing right away it is ready.)Then I just followed directions for the rolls or I made loaves. Thank you again. Know my kids only want mom's bread and not store bought bread. We all had fun making it.

This is designed for a bread machine which I don't have. I made this in my Kitchenaid stand mixer. I use grams for measurements because there are no 100% accurate measuring cups I'm aware of and weight is the same in my kitchen as anyone else. So bread flour weighs 120g cup so 2 3/4 cup is 330g Wheat flour weighs 112g using King Arthur Golden Wheat weighs 28g per 1/4 cup x 4 = 112g. I heated up the milk and honey to 110-115 deg. Added the yeast that I increased to 1 1/2 tsp or 1/2 Tbs and let sit for 10min. I mixed the bread and whole wheat flour in my kitchen aid mixer and added the salt. I then added the beaten egg and softened butter to the yeast mixture before pouring into the stand mixer and using the bread hook I turned on the machine to 4. After scraping it all down I ended up adding 2 additional Tbs of bread flour and 1 whole wheat before the dough came together and pulled away from the bowl and was tacky but didn't stick to my fingers. I took the dough out and weighed it and the weight of the dough mixture was 890g. I took a short cut instead of rolling it out to some thickness I divided the dough into the number of rolls I wanted which was 10. I cut out 89 grams of dough and rolled them on my counter lightly dusted with flour into round balls. I then placed them on a slightly greased cookie sheet. I then flattened them slightly. After all 10 rolls were in place and flattened slightly I covered with a tea towel. I have a bread proof feature on my oven so I turned that on which is 110deg. After about 90 min they had risen enough to bake. Removed them and preheated the oven to 350deg. Baked the rolls at 350 for about 15 min. I started at 11 min and kept going until they were to the desired color. I then brushed them all with melted butter. These are incredibly soft and delicious. I have made these numerous times that this is my final outcome. If you want larger then divide the total weight by less and if you want more divide by less. Each of my rolls are 89-90 grams maybe slightly less then a butternut hamburger bun.

These were very good! I have a bit of experience with yeast, but it's been awhile. I made these as rolls for a dinner party, and they were light in texture and delicious. I used my stand mixer with two packets of regular yeast and AP flour instead of bread flour. I proofed the yeast in the warm milk, then added the butter and egg, then added the combined dry ingredients to the mixer bowl, one heaping tablespoon at a time. After one rise, I formed into informal balls and placed in greased muffin tins. Since they were risen well before dinner, I partially baked until some structure developed, then interrupted the baking. I finished them later with my convection oven. Nice, tender rolls with a good crust. Thanks for the idea!

Thanks Angie for the suggestions 
Used only Multigrain Fluor and worked awesome
Put the dough hook on warm the milk and honey, proof the yeast for 10 min., add the eggs and butter, measure all dry ingredients in a bowl and whisk to make sure distributed, slowly add flour mix in 3 batches.
Then I knead with the standmixer 7-10min.
To make sure gluten is developed take a golf ball sized piece of dough and stretch in opposite directions using your thumb and forefinger of both hand. If it stretches thin enough to see light through without it tearing right away it is ready

Soft, fluffy, tasty. They are a wonderful hamburger bun replacement. I add crushed flax seeds to mine. If you want them truly airy, let the dough rise twice before shaping it into buns. Also, molasses is a good substitution for the honey if you want them a little less sweet, and darker.

Soft tender inside, nice crust. I have made these with water or milk . Good I either way. I don't brush with melted butter as I find that makes them too sticky. I brush them with egg white , makes a nice brown crusts. I needed to bake them for 25 minutes. A very versatile roll

These are phenomenal! Made the first time with my bread machine. Made into hamburger buns. Used 1 cup white flour and 3 cups of whole wheat. Used olive oil in place of butter and a whole pkg of yeast. Used corn meal on cookie sheet instead of greasing it.
Getting ready to make them again with 1 1/2 cup white flour and 2 1/2 cups of whole wheat. Going to try them in my new kitchen aid stand up mixer and make them into hot dog buns this time. YUM YUM my husband and I are both eagerly anticipating these with brats in them for dinner.

These are such tasty rolls! I did omit the butter after removing from oven (personal preference) and used virgin coconut oil and vegg in the dough in stead of butter and eggs, respectively. I used my stand mixer in stead of bread machine and proofed the dough in the oven on proof setting.

I made them a little smaller than suggested and didn’t add any salt because I am on a low sodium diet. They didn’t rise as much as I had hoped but they taste great! I will definitely be making again but will roll them thicker next time.
Great recipe for sandwich buns. Only thing I changed was increasing the yeast to 1-1/2 tsp. I let them rise for about 1 hr and 15 mins then baked for a full 15 mins.

I used the bread machine and rapid rise yeast and they were done in no time. I did find that the 350° oven had to be adjusted. Once I had baked them 13 minutes they were still not browning so I turned the oven to 375 and added another three minutes. They came out perfectly. Great recipe! I made hamburger and hotdog buns with them.

This recipe is scrumptious! I never liked anything made with wheat flour. This has a combination which likely helped. I have a white bun recipe that I thought couldn't be topped but this one is my go to now. I've made them several times & always freeze them. They are just as yummy after freezing. I've used them for burgers, egg salad, tuna, chicken salad & deli sandwiches.

This recipe was different before, and great then with the changes I made that are now in the current recipe. These include using milk instead of water and using bread flour instead of all purpose. This is one of my go to recipes for making a loaf. I had the same problem as another reviewer getting the buns to rise. They suggested more yeast so I'll try that. I also love the idea of making hoagie rolls out of this. I now also use sprouted wheat which is much healthier than whole grain whole wheat. This recipe is so good I've been making it for over 20 yrs. Go ahead and try it, you will LOVE it.
Rolls were great. Picture is bad I know lol. My son is very picky and he loves them. This is a keeper. Thank you!
I don't have a bread machine but I followed what Angie said In the comments .Came out perfect my kids eat them faster than I can make them.
Making these for the 2nd time today... first time they were incredible! Hoping they come out just as good. Just follow the recipe- but in back of my mind- considering how I can double it.

Great rolls make them almost every time we have burgers. Easy to make.... love the fact they are rolled out and cut rather than shaping individually.
I decreased the water by 1/4 cup, used 1T. Bread machine yeast and 1 t. Kosher salt. Yielded 12 large 80 g. (2.8 oz.) Rolls. Next time I'll add 1/2 T. Vital wheat gluten.
